subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the formula of the ionic compound aluminium oxide, from Al³⁺ and O²⁻?
What is the relative formula mass (Mr) of water, H2O? (Ar: H=1, O=16)
What is the formula of the compound formed from Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions?
questions.explain: Two Cl⁻ ions balance one Mg²⁺ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: How many moles are in 80 g of NaOH? (Mr = 40)
A solution contains 20 g of solute in 0.5 dm³. What is its concentration in g/dm³?
A reaction has a theoretical yield of 50 g but only 40 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution with 0.5 mol of solute in 2 dm³?
Atom economy is a measure of:
options: The proportion of reactant atoms that become the desired product
questions.explain: Atom economy measures how much of the reactants' mass ends up as useful product.

questions.q: Balance: N2 + ?H2 → 2NH3. What number goes in front of H2?
questions.explain: 3H2 gives 6 H atoms, matching 2NH3 (6 H), and N2 gives 2 N.

questions.q: What is the Mr of carbon dioxide, CO2? (Ar: C=12, O=16)
A compound contains 0.2 mol carbon and 0.4 mol hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.2:0.4 simplifies to 1:2, giving CH2.

questions.q: Approximately how many particles are in one mole of a substance (Avogadro's constant)?
